68519-the-urine-dance-of-the-zuni-indian.title: Zuni Indians Of New Mexico
68519-the-urine-dance-of-the-zuni-indian.creator: Unknown
68519-the-urine-dance-of-the-zuni-indian.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. into the hair at top of head and ears. Several wore, in addition to the tortoise-shell rattles, strings of brass sleigh-bells at knees. One was more grotesquely attired than the rest in a long India-rubber gossamer “over all” and a pair of goggles, painted white, over his eyes. His general “get-up” was a spirited take-off upon a Mexican priest.

arxiv-2011-11475.title: The Hund’s Superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As
arxiv-2011-11475.creator: H. Miao, Y. L. Wang, J.-X. Yin, J. Zhang, S. Zhang, M. Z. Hasan, R. Yang, X. C. Wang, C. Q. Jin, T. Qian, H. Ding, H.-L. Lee, G. Kotliar
arxiv-2011-11475.description: Abstract We combine transport, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and scanning tunneling spectroscopy to investigate several low energy manifestations of the Hund coupling in a canonical FeSC family Li(Fe,Co)As. We determine the doping dependence of the coherent-incoherent crossover temperature and the quasi-particle effective mass enhancement in the normal state.

arxiv-2105-06626.title: Near- and far-field expansions for stationary solutions of Poisson–Nernst–Planck equations Due to inelegant symbol, we provide an original manuscript in arXiv.
arxiv-2105-06626.creator: Jhih-Hong Lyu, Chiun-Chang Lee, Tai-Chia Lin
arxiv-2105-06626.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jhih-Hong Lyu, Chiun-Chang Lee, Tai-Chia Lin. This work is concerned with the stationary Poisson–Nernst–Planck equation with a large parameter which describes a huge number of ions occupying an electrolytic region. Firstly, we focus on the model with a single specie of positive charges in one-dimensional bounded domains due to the assumption that these ions are transported in the same direction along a tubular-like mircodomain, as was introduced in [ 2 ] .

arxiv-2207-07035.title: Characterizing Nodes and Edges in Dynamic Attributed Networks: A Social-based Approach
arxiv-2207-07035.creator: Thiago H. P. Silva, Alberto H. F. Laender, Pedro O. S. Vaz de Melo
arxiv-2207-07035.description: Abstract . How to characterize nodes and edges in dynamic attributed networks based on social aspects? We address this problem by exploring the strength of the ties between actors and their associated attributes over time, thus capturing the social roles of the actors and the meaning of their dynamic interactions in different social network scenarios.

arxiv-2208-06211.title: CUSP: a two cubesats constellation for Space Weather and solar flares X-ray polarimetry
arxiv-2208-06211.creator: Sergio Fabiani, Ilaria Baffo, Sergio Bonomo, Gessica Contini, Enrico Costa, Giovanni Cucinella, Giovanni De Cesare, Ettore Del Monte, Andrea Del Re, Sergio Di Cosimo, Simone Di Filippo, Alessandro Di Marco, Pierluigi Fanelli, Fabio La Monaca, Alfredo Locarini, Pasqualino Loffredo, Giovanni Lombardi,
arxiv-2208-06211.description: Abstract The CUbesat Solar Polarimeter (CUSP) project aims to develop a constellation of two CubeSats orbiting the Earth to measure the linear polarisation of solar flares in the hard X-ray band by means of a Compton scattering polarimeter on board of each satellite. CUSP will allow to study the magnetic reconnection and particle acceleration in the flaring magnetic structures.

arxiv-2211-14243.title: Investigation of Airy equations with random initial conditions
arxiv-2211-14243.description: Abstract The paper investigates properties of mean-square solutions to the Airy equation with random initial data given by stationary processes. The result on the modulus of continiuty of the solution is stated and properties of the covariance function are described. Bounds for the distributions of the suprema of solutions under φ \varphi -sub-Gaussian initial conditions are presented.

arxiv-2304-01534.title: FedBEVT: Federated Learning Bird’s Eye View Perception Transformer in Road Traffic Systems
arxiv-2304-01534.creator: Rui Song, Runsheng Xu, Andreas Festag, Jiaqi Ma, Alois Knoll
arxiv-2304-01534.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rui Song, Runsheng Xu, Andreas Festag, Jiaqi Ma, Alois Knoll. Bird’s eye view (BEV) perception is becoming increasingly important in the field of autonomous driving. It uses multi-view camera data to learn a transformer model that directly projects the perception of the road environment onto the BEV perspective. However, training a transformer model often requires a large amount of data, and as camera data for road traffic are often private, they are typically not shared.

arxiv-2308-07486.title: O-1: Self-training with Oracle and 1-best Hypothesis
arxiv-2308-07486.creator: Murali Karthick Baskar, Andrew Rosenberg, Bhuvana Ramabhadran, Kartik Audhkhasi
arxiv-2308-07486.description: Abstract We introduce O-1, a new self-training objective to reduce training bias and unify training and evaluation metrics for speech recognition. O-1 is a faster variant of Expected Minimum Bayes Risk (EMBR), that boosts the oracle hypothesis and can accommodate both supervised and unsupervised data.

arxiv-2405-12024.title: Polynomials and algebraic curves related to certain binary and b b -ary overpartitions Thanks: Research supported in part by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada, Grant # 145628481
arxiv-2405-12024.creator: Karl Dilcher, Larry Ericksen
arxiv-2405-12024.description: Abstract . We begin by considering a sequence of polynomials in three variables whose coefficients count restricted binary overpartitions with certain properties. We then concentrate on two specific subsequences that are closely related to the Chebyshev polynomials of both kinds, deriving combinatorial and algebraic properties of some special cases.

arxiv-2407-09196.title: Testing volume integrals of travel-time sensitivity kernels for flows
arxiv-2407-09196.creator: Michal Švanda, Daniel Chmúrny
arxiv-2407-09196.description: Abstract Context. Helioseismic inversions rely largely on sensitivity kernels, 3-D spatial functions describing how do the changes in the solar interior translate into the changes of helioseismic observables. These sensitivity kernels come in most cases from the forward modelling utilising state-of-the-art solar models. Aims.

arxiv-2411-10906.title: Efficient, Low-Regret, Online Reinforcement Learning for Linear MDPs
arxiv-2411-10906.creator: Philips George John, Arnab Bhattacharyya, Silviu Maniu, Dimitrios Myrisiotis, Zhenan Wu
arxiv-2411-10906.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning algorithms are usually stated without theoretical guarantees regarding their performance. Recently, Jin, Yang, Wang, and Jordan (COLT 2020) showed a polynomial-time reinforcement learning algorithm (namely, LSVI-UCB) for the setting of linear Markov decision processes, and provided theoretical guarantees regarding its running time and regret.

arxiv-2505-13075.title: Tabletop Lensless Imaging in the Extreme Ultraviolet with Reduced Radiation Dose
arxiv-2505-13075.creator: Sukyoon Oh, Monalisa Mallick, Thomas Siefke, Christian Spielmann
arxiv-2505-13075.description: Abstract High-resolution extreme ultraviolet (XUV) imaging remains limited by conventional approaches that require complex optics such as multilayer mirrors and zone plates. These methods are expensive, suffer from chromatic aberrations and narrow fields of view, and demand highly stable, coherent beam sources typically found only at large-scale facilities.

arxiv-2507-08806.title: Think Clearly: Improving Reasoning via Redundant Token Pruning
arxiv-2507-08806.creator: Daewon Choi, Jimin Lee, Jihoon Tack, Woomin Song, Saket Dingliwal, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Bhavana Ganesh, Jinwoo Shin, Aram Galstyan, Sravan Babu Bodapati
arxiv-2507-08806.description: Abstract Recent large language models have shown promising capabilities in long-form reasoning, following structured chains of thought before arriving at a final answer. However, we observe that these reasoning paths tend to include substantial redundancy; analyzing attention patterns reveals that attention scores are widely scattered, particularly incorrect answers exhibit greater attention sparsity.

arxiv-2509-08417.title: Probing one–loop–induced decay channel H ± → W ± ​ γ H^{\pm}\to W^{\pm}\gamma in the Two Higgs Doublet Models at muon–TeV colliders
arxiv-2509-08417.creator: Dzung Tri Tran, Quang Hoang-Minh Pham, Khoa Ngo-Thanh Ho, Khiem Hong Phan
arxiv-2509-08417.description: Abstract In this work, we study the one–loop–induced decay channel H ± → W ± ​ γ H^{\pm}\rightarrow W^{\pm}\gamma in the general ℛ ξ \mathcal{R}_{\xi} gauge within Two Higgs Doublet Models. We analytically verify the gauge invariance ( ξ \xi -independence), ultraviolet finiteness, and renormalization-scale independence of the one-loop form factors, thereby confirming the consistency of our calculations.

britannica-1911-cactus.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-cactus.description: Article 'Cactus' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 4), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. beautiful flowers, and are now so popular in our gardens that the name has become familiar. It is one of the few Linnaean generic terms which have been entirely set aside by the names adopted for the modern divisions of the group.

pmc-10607036.creator: Gwenny T L Janssen, Jos I M Egger, Roy P C Kessels, Antonio Vita
pmc-10607036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). (1) Background: chronic alcohol use is consistently associated with impaired executive functioning, but its profile across the spectrum from mild to major alcohol-related cognitive impairment is, to date, unclear. This study aims to compare executive performances of patients with alcohol-induced neurocognitive disorder, including Korsakoff’s syndrome (KS), by using a computerized assessment battery allowing a fine-grained and precise neuropsychological assessment; (2) Methods: performances of 22 patients with alcohol-related cognitive impairment (ARCI) and 20 patients with KS were compared to those of 22 matched

pmc-10630117.title: Trans-scaphoid trans-lunate trans-triquetral volar perilunate dislocation: A case report
pmc-10630117.creator: K El Khaymy, O Fadili, A Chrak, Y Bouzid, E El Hamzaoui, O El Adaoui, Y El Andaloussi, D Bennouna, M Fadili
pmc-10630117.description: IntroductionTranslunate volar perilunate dislocations are extremely rare, with few documented cases. Only eight instances of volar translunate perilunate dislocation have been described in the literature. This report presents a successfully treated case using early reduction and internal fixation that led to a very satisfying outcome at 9 months follow-up.

pmc-11359882.title: Genomic Sequence of Streptococcus salivarius MDI13 and Latilactobacillus sakei MEI5: Two Promising Probiotic Strains Isolated from European Hakes (Merluccius merluccius, L.)
pmc-11359882.creator: Lara Díaz-Formoso, Diogo Contente, Javier Feito, Pablo E Hernández, Juan Borrero, Estefanía Muñoz-Atienza, Luis M Cintas, Alessandra Pelagalli
pmc-11359882.description: Simple SummaryIn fish farming, diseases have commonly been fought with the abusive use of antibiotics, which have caused antibiotic (multi)resistances in bacteria. Consequently, it is necessary to explore safe and environmentally friendly alternative approaches to improve the fish health and avoid the treatment of bacterial diseases with antibiotics such as the use of probiotics.

pmc-11399561.title: A novel lncRNA GM47544 modulates triglyceride metabolism by inducing ubiquitination-dependent protein degradation of APOC3
pmc-11399561.creator: Qianqian Xiao, Luyun Wang, Jing Wang, Man Wang, Dao Wen Wang, Hu Ding
pmc-11399561.description: ObjectiveEmerging evidence highlights the pivotal roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in lipid metabolism. Apoprotein C3 (ApoC3) is a well-established therapeutic target for hypertriglyceridemia and exhibits a strong association with cardiovascular disease. However, the exact mechanisms via which the lncRNAs control ApoC3 expression remain unclear.MethodsWe identified a novel long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), GM47544, within the ApoA1/C3/A4/A5 gene cluster.

pmc-11539037.title: Low temperature synthesis of franklinite stabilized cefixime as a multifunctional nanoformulation
pmc-11539037.creator: Amna Munsaf, Muhammad Naeem Ahmed, Aroosa Zafar, Bilal Akram, Mahmoud A. A. Ibrahim
pmc-11539037.description: Cefixime, an antibiotic with low solubility, stability, bioavailability and therapeutic effectiveness, needs to be administered in larger doses for effective treatment. This can lead to higher healthcare costs and increased risk of side effects, negatively affecting public health. Herein, we aim to develop a strategy to overcome the aforementioned limitations by stabilizing it using franklinite nanostructures.

pmc-11638444.title: Unveiling the Potential of Cyclin-Dependent Kinases 4 and 6 Inhibitors Beyond Progression in Hormone Receptor Positive/Human Epidermal Growth Factor Negative Advanced Breast Cancer – A Clinical Review
pmc-11638444.creator: Chiara Benvenuti, Thomas Grinda, Elie Rassy, Julia Dixon-Douglas, Joana M. Ribeiro, Alberto Zambelli, Armando Santoro, Barbara Pistilli
pmc-11638444.description: Opinion StatementCyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) have revolutionized the management of hormone receptor-positive (HR +) breast cancer. However, resistance to CDK4/6i remains an unavoidable challenge, with limited evidence to guide the choice of subsequent treatments. Continuation of CDK4/6 inhibition raises as a compelling treatment option and is currently an active area of research.

pmc-11691544.title: LOVE HURTS: MARITAL STATUS AND CHRONIC PAIN
pmc-11691544.creator: S Emily Choi, Brandon Wagner
pmc-11691544.description: While chronic pain is a highly prevalent and costly public health concern among older adults in the United States, longitudinal research on the social determinants of chronic pain, particularly its association with social relationships, has been limited. To address this gap, this study investigates how marital status influences later-life chronic pain with a focus on gender-specific variations.

pmc-12492728.title: Recurrent Acute Kidney Injury Due to Atheroembolic Renal Disease: Diagnostic Utility of Fundoscopy
pmc-12492728.creator: Shiyun Tan, Nigel Fong, Cai Jiashen, Debajyoti Roy
pmc-12492728.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Atheroembolic renal disease (AERD) is a rare and often underdiagnosed cause of acute kidney injury (AKI), particularly in patients with atherosclerotic disease. We present the case of a 66-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) (baseline creatinine 100-120 μmol/L) who developed AKI after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), followed by recurrent episodes and progressive renal decline despite no further invasive procedures.

pmc-12755229.title: Comparison of Prostate-Specific Antigen Response in Black Patients with Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer Initiated on Apalutamide vs Abiraterone Acetate
pmc-12755229.creator: Gordon Brown, Sabree Burbage, Ibrahim Khilfeh, Carmine Rossi, Shawn Du, Frederic Kinkead, Lilian Diaz, Dominic Pilon, Benjamin Lowentritt
pmc-12755229.description: BackgroundImproved clinical outcomes have been observed in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) who experience deep prostate-specific antigen (PSA) responses after treatment with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs).ObjectiveThis retrospective longitudinal study aimed to compare real-world PSA90 response (≥90% reduction from pretreatment levels) in Black patients with mCSPC treated with apalutamide vs abiraterone acetate.

pmc-12837066.title: CHI3L1 promotes cell division through activation of RhoA in lung cancer cells
pmc-12837066.creator: Ji Eun Yu, Jung-Hyun Shim, In Jun Yeo, Dong Ju Son, Jaesuk Yun, Key-Hwan Lim, Hanseul Park, Yoon Seok Roh, Sang-Bae Han, Jin Tae Hong
pmc-12837066.description: BackgroundCytokinesis, the final stage of cell division, is crucial for maintaining genomic stability. Dysregulation of cytokinesis can contribute to cancer development. This study aimed to investigate the role of CHI3L1 in cytokinesis and its influence on lung cancer cell growth.

pmc-13291340.title: Impact of the 2024 Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network Kidney Donor Profile Index Rescoring on Donor Kidney Utilization and Allocation out of Sequence: A one‐Year Analysis
pmc-13291340.creator: Shengliang He, Christie P Thomas, Alan I Reed
pmc-13291340.description: BackgroundIn October 2024, the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) removed hepatitis C virus (HCV) positivity and African American/Black (AA/B) donor race from the Kidney Donor Profile Index (KDPI) calculation. This study evaluates the early impact of this policy change on kidney utilization during its first year.

pmc-13317662.creator: Mateja Jankovic Makek, Ena Tolic, Christoph Lange, Matea Zvonar, Dora Darapi Marušić, Ivana Marekovic, Sonja Badovinac, Goran Glodic, Kristijan Marcic, Nika Zielinski, Maja Reimann

pmc-13337592.title: Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI for identifying dopamine transporter imaging abnormality risk in idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
pmc-13337592.creator: Jae Rim Kim, Beomseok Sohn, Jeong Won Jo, Hwan Heo, Soohwa Song, Eung Yeop Kim, Eun Yeon Joo
pmc-13337592.description: Neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging (NM-MRI) enables non-invasive assessment of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc). However, its utility in identifying dopaminergic dysfunction in idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) remains unclear. This study evaluated NM-MRI alterations in the SNpc, stratified by dopamine transporter (DaT) imaging status, to assess its performance in detecting early dopaminergic alterations.

pmc-13608636.title: Towards a Conceptual Framework for Mechanical Dose in Skeletal Muscle: Integrating Mechanobiology and Resistance Training
pmc-13608636.creator: Pedro Morouço
pmc-13608636.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite major advances in exercise physiology, biomechanics, and mechanobiology, exercise science still lacks a clear conceptual definition of the mechanical stimulus experienced by skeletal muscle during resistance training. Current approaches rely on diverse external, internal, and biomechanical variables (e.g., volume-load, force, power, velocity, time under tension, or muscle architecture), yet none individually captures the muscle-specific mechanical exposure relevant to muscular adaptation. This conceptual inconsistency limits comparisons across studies, complicates training prescription, and hinders the development of individualized monitoring strategies.
